Methodology
  • Each dot is an AIMC sub-category , grouped exactly as in Portfolio Analysts. Position = median across its funds, one share class per fund.
  • X = latest NAV ÷ MA125 − 1; Y = latest NAV ÷ MA20 − 1. MA = simple mean of the last 20 / 125 NAV observations (trading days).
  • Strong above both; Pullback above MA125, below MA20; Recovery below MA125, above MA20; Weak below both.
  • Normal moves follow the clockwise cycle Recovery → Strong → Pullback → Weak → Recovery, so the previous zone is implied. A small white V on a dot marks a category that jumped or moved against that cycle (counter-clockwise or across the diagonal) within the lookback period. The open side of the V faces the quadrant it came from (e.g. opening downward = it came from the zone below); the table also lists the previous zone. With lookback above 0, categories that stayed in the same zone are removed from the chart (shown greyed in the table); at 0 every category is shown.
  • Tail (on hover only): the hovered dot\'s historical position as a fading line, from a hollow start dot (Tail length trading days ago) to today. Category view uses the median of its funds on each date; Fund view the fund itself. Tail length follows the Zone-change lookback automatically (adjust the Tail slider afterwards if you want a different length). Click dots to keep their tails shown (several at once, e.g. to compare two categories); click a dot again to release it, Esc releases all. Length is limited by the NAV history left after the Slow MA window.
  • Funds with stale NAV (>7 days) or fewer NAV observations than the Slow MA window are excluded (young funds appear when Slow MA is set shorter, minimum 50); categories with fewer than 3 funds are not shown. Raw NAV, not dividend-adjusted.
Source: SEC Thailand Open API (sec_data.sqlite); AIMC categories as in Portfolio Analysts. Data as of 20 Nov 2026 · Generated 21 Nov 2026. Not investment advice.
